rv.q: Such is my enthusiasm for Kokandy Productions' exquisite little Chicago staging of Stephen Sondheim's "Sunday in the Park with George" that I wrote down five different opening paragraphs, or organizing principles, if you will.

This time, it’s a richly emotional, cleverly designed and musically vivid “Sunday in the Park with George,” about the creation of painter Georges Seurat’s “A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte,” the large neo-impressionist masterpiece that — so very lucky for us! — hangs a few miles away in the Art Institute.
This show must be included on Chicago's must-see list for the Autumn season.
If the first act of Sunday in the Park with George is perfect (you heard me: it's perfect), the second is… a bit clunkier.
Rather than aiming for utmost fidelity to the 'Sundays' that have come before it, Kokandy opts to create their own signature production that will be remembered as one of Chicago's best.
Kokandy Productions welcomes the audience into a mesmerizing experience that will engulf them into the show's artistry and emotions.
Go see it. Always see 'Sunday in the Park with George' and always support storefront theatre.
Webb captures George's obsessive artistic drive with a fervor that's palpable, pulling the audience into his orbit and keeping it rapt throughout.
It takes a strong cast and a loving Director/Choreographer like Derek Van Barham to pull off Sunday In the Park with George and Kokandy Productions gives us this in spades.

Sunday in the Park with George is reservedly recommended. Those who are avowed fans of Stephen Sondheim and/or Kokandy Productions will certainly enjoy the show. But, if this is your first experience with the musical, it is advised that you wait to see it in a more appropriate space.
Kokandy's Sunday in the Park with George succeeds because it recognizes and embraces that the musical is more than the story of Georges Seurat and the making of a famous painting.
They worked it to absolute perfection, including the Act One ending where the painting comes to life! WOW!
Kokandy Productions brings this challenging musical to life with a strong cast, thoughtful direction and an appreciation for the questions at its heart.
Kevin Webb as George himself shows us a deeply emotional and dedicated artist, even if George himself can't show it.

Ultimately Lapine and Sondheim's opus is a theatrical tour deforce with perhaps a few hiccups that is a favorite among sophisticated theater goers who are open to experiencing a challenging score — in this case performed terrifically with great vocals and instrumentation.
